transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-12
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Miller (AE), Priya Shah (SE), Evan Park (Enablement), Jordan Lee (Training), Sam Torres (AE), Maya Chen (SE), Liam O'Brien (Sales)

Summary:
Quick enablement session focused on messaging, competitive positioning vs OpenAI/Anthropic, and two demo practice runs with live feedback. Emphasis on how to handle latency/cost questions, Dedicated vs Hosted positioning, and security/SSO/KMS talking points. Action items assigned for slide deck, demo recording, and battlecards.

Topics:
- Core pitch: high-level messaging for product-market fit and where Redwood sits
- Competitive differentiators: runtime performance, cost controls, private deployment
- Demo walkthrough: prepared cold-start demo and a customer scenario (e-commerce product search reranking)
- Objection handling: latency vs cost tradeoffs, SOC2/ISO, VPC/on-prem
- Practice Q&A and riffing with customers

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Miller: Alright everybody, good afternoon—thanks for joining. We'll kick off, this is the SE enablement, messaging plus demo practice. Evan, can you run timing?
[00:12] Evan Park: Yep, got it. We're scheduled for an hour, plan to leave ten minutes for q's at the end.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Cool. Quick agenda: 1) 15 min messaging review, 2) competitive positioning 10-ish, 3) two demo runs with feedback. Trying to keep this practical.
[00:31] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Also want to surface the new battlecard request, especially for Anthropic. We keep getting that ask.
[00:38] Sam Torres: FYI I've had a couple prospects push back on hosted vs dedicated cost. Would be great to practice that.
[00:45] Alex Miller: Perfect—Priya, take us through the core messaging.
[00:48] Priya Shah: Yep. So top-line: Redwood is a developer-first inference platform that lets teams run LLMs with predictable latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private environments. The thing we push is inference as a first-class runtime—so not just model access, it's serving.
[01:05] Priya Shah: Quick talking points: one, unified API across envs; two, production controls—batching, KV caching, quantization profiles that change unit economics; three, reliability fallbacks and routing policies.
[01:22] Maya Chen: Quick Q—when a customer says 'what's the difference between Redwood and OpenAI for model access', what's the one-liner?
[01:28] Priya Shah: Good. One-liner: OpenAI exposes models and model capabilities; Redwood provides the serving runtime and ops controls to make those models predictable and economical in production. So we emphasize operational guarantees.
[01:40] Sam Torres: And if they ask about latency—customers sometimes say 'OpenAI seems faster' — what's the play?
[01:45] Priya Shah: Two-part: for raw single-request latency, cloud-managed endpoints can be competitive; we lean on our Dedicated offering for predictable tail-latency at scale and on smart routing/fallback to keep p99s low. Also highlight prefix/KV caching and hardware choices that affect steady-state throughput.
[02:02] Alex Miller: Don't forget to call out our cost levers; customers love seeing batching and quantization recommendations reduce token cost by X. Use concrete examples in deck.
[02:10] Evan Park: Noted—add cost example slide.
[02:13] Jordan Lee: There's often confusion around KV cache vs K-V cash—lol—so we should make that plain.
[02:18] Priya Shah: Yes, we should show a small diagram: KV cache stores previous prefixes to avoid recomputing so it's huge for chat-heavy workloads.
[02:28] Liam O'Brien: Ok demo practice—Sam you said you wanted to run a hosted vs dedicated scenario?
[02:33] Sam Torres: Yeah I can lead the first demo. I'm going to pretend I'm talking to a mid-market e-commerce shop that needs fast product search with reranking and privacy controls.
[02:42] Alex Miller: Good. Use the 'low-lift integration' angle first. Remember to ask about their throughput and data residency constraints.
[02:50] [02:50] Demo run 1 (Sam as AE, Priya on demo):
[02:50] Sam Torres: Hi, thanks for taking the time. We're an e-comm company, about 200 rps at peak, lots of PII in logs, need 99th percentile latency under 200ms, and cost per thousand tokens is a concern. What's Redwood look like?
[03:10] Priya Shah: Great question. So you'd start by picking a hosted model for quick time to value, then as you validate workload you can move to Dedicated for predictable throughput. We also offer private deployment if data residency is required.
[03:24] Priya Shah: For latency, if you need p99 under 200ms at 200 rps we'd recommend a dedicated GPU pool + smart routing; we'd also enable KV caching for conversational workloads. For cost, we show batching & quantization recs to cut cost by up to 60% in some cases.
[03:42] Sam Torres: Customer asks about encryption and key management—are keys in their tenant?
[03:47] Priya Shah: Yes, for Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys and audit logs; we also have SOC2 and ISO compliance docs.
[03:58] [03:58] Feedback (group):
[03:58] Alex Miller: Good flow. Two notes: ask more about request size distribution—are they short queries or long contexts? Also when you say 60% cost reduction, tie to an example (e.g., sample X with quantization Q8 + batching).
[04:18] Evan Park: Also slip in the console observability bit—token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
[04:25] Sam Torres: Got it. Thanks.
[04:27] [04:27] Demo run 2 (Maya leads, Priya demoing technical bits):
[04:27] Maya Chen: I'll take a more technical buyer angle—customer cares about KV cache coherence and model rollouts.
[04:33] Priya Shah: Demo: show runtime dashboard, model rollout canary config, and fallback policies.
[04:40] Maya Chen: On the canary—how do you validate that a new model doesn't regress quality?
[04:45] Priya Shah: We tie rollouts to eval sets and prompt-level regression alerts; you can configure canary traffic and automatic rollback if quality drops. Also we keep input/output logs for auditing (redacted as needed).
[04:58] Maya Chen: The buyer asks about auditability—SSO, RBAC?
[05:03] Priya Shah: We support SSO/SAML, granular RBAC, and long-term audit log retention as an add-on. For Private you can plug in your SIEM.
[05:12] [05:12] Feedback (group):
[05:12] Alex Miller: Nice technical depth. Two minor points: be careful when you say 'we keep logs'—clarify retention and redaction options, customers ask a lot about PII.
[05:24] Jordan Lee: Also highlight the differentiator: unified runtime + ops vs just model access. That's the recurring theme.
[05:31] Evan Park: Quick competitive practice—someone throw an objection: 'Why not just use OpenAI and a homegrown caching layer?'
[05:39] Priya Shah: Answer: you can, but it takes months to build and maintain; we offer prebuilt operational primitives (continuous batching, KV cache, quantization profiles, routing policies) and support to keep production SLOs. Plus cost predictability with Dedicated.
[05:55] Sam Torres: Another objection: 'Anthropic has strong safety models'—how do we handle safety framing?
[06:02] Priya Shah: Acknowledge Anthropic's strengths; then pivot to how we enable safe deployments across models—tooling for filters, evals, and rapid rollbacks. It's about enabling reliable ops around models, not replacing model-level safety research.
[06:20] Alex Miller: Quick note on language—the term 'quant' sometimes confuses customers. Say 'quantization' and give 1-line description.
[06:29] [06:29] Q&A and edge cases:
[06:29] Liam O'Brien: What if a customer insists on on-prem for compliance—how early in the sales cycle do we bring in Private?
[06:37] Priya Shah: If they mention regulated data or residency within discovery, introduce Private early and loop in solutions. Mention that Private has longer lead-time and requires infra planning.
[06:48] Jordan Lee: Any quick tips for handling procurement/legal RFPs?
[06:52] Alex Miller: Have the SOC2/ISO artifacts handy, provide standard contract language; push for pilot with defined success criteria to accelerate procurement.
[07:05] Evan Park: Ok we have ten minutes left—let's do lightning rounds: each person run a 60s objection/response. Sam?
[07:12] Sam Torres: 'We're worried about token cost'—response: show cost levers + share a sample cost calc with quant/batching.
[07:22] Maya Chen: 'How do you manage large KV caches across instances?'—response: explain sharding/eviction and prefix caching strategies.
[07:33] Liam O'Brien: 'Latency spikes during black friday'—response: suggest Dedicated with burst capacity, routing policies and fallback models.
[07:44] Alex Miller: Nice. Final recap: action items (see slide), we'll share the recording and you all should schedule mock demos.
[07:54] Jordan Lee: Two asks: please make the battlecard concise with buy/neutral/sell points vs OpenAI/Anthropic; and add one slide that maps customer persona to pitch.
[08:05] Alex Miller: Will do. Thanks everyone.

End of meeting. Recording saved to enablement/shared/2026-11-12-se-enablement-2026-11-12.mp4. Deck link: https://redwood.app/drive/enablement/decks/se-messaging-2026-11-12.pdf. Competitive spreadsheet link: https://redwood.app/drive/enablement/competitive-battlecards.xlsx
